newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Nomura to launch PTCL $150 mln convertible bond.
newsitem.headline: Nomura to launch PTCL $150 mln convertible bond.

text.p: Nomura International plc will soon float a $150 million five-year bond convertible into shares of the state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd (PTCL), according to a Nomura letter received on Wednesday.
The letter from London-based Nomura addressed to Karachi Stock Exchange president Arif Habib said the issue would be launched with a road show on Wednesday in London.
"The books for the transaction will open later this week and will be closed shortly after the Singapore road show," the letter made available to Reuters said.
The road show will continue in London on Thursday and will then go on to Edinburgh on Friday, Hong Kong on Monday and conclude on Tuesday in Singapore, the letter said.
It said the dollar-denominated bonds would be exchangeable into fully paid "A" shares of PTCL held by Pakistan government.
In 1994, the government floated PTCL's 12 percent stake domestically in the form of common stock and abroad as global depositary receipts (GDRs).
The five-year maturity bond will have a coupon rate indicated at six percent payable semi-annually with an issuer call option at par from February 2000.
The issue also has a three-year investors' put option at a price to yield 150 basis points above the three-year U.S. treasuries.
The bond would be listed at the Luxembourg Stock Exchange and the investor will have the option to exchange them into common stock listed in Pakistani bourses or into GDRs.
The transaction's lead managers are Nomura International plc and Union Bank of Switzerland (East Asia) Ltd, the letter said.
PTCL on Wednesday dropped one rupee ($0.02) to 35 rupees at the Karachi Stock Exchange.
